title: Nosy Alañaña Light
visualBrief: Slender eight-sided concrete taper with staggered arched window rows, worn pale lower shaft and dark upper daymark, strong eight gallery consoles, octagonal concrete balustrade, round lantern and domed cap. Broad stepped entrance podium and flat projecting door canopy.

sourceFacts.basis: APMF operator2020 ministerial visit explicitly gives60m height and photographs the doorway, concrete landing steps and lantern. Original2023 Riaan Wessels and2006 Maxsnet exterior photographs establish octagonal taper, staggered arches, upper dark band, concrete gallery and domed cap. Widths and intermediate elevations are photograph proportions.
sourceFacts.reviewScope: Static concrete-tower exterior using2006/2020/2023 research. APMF publishes60m height;7.1m base flats, window spacing, gallery/consoles and canopy are photo-proportioned. Pale lower shaft/dark upper band represents the older documented paint design through common plaster; variable heavy2023 staining is not copied as a texture. Interior stair, lamp operation, detached keeper buildings, foliage and current restoration condition are outside scope. Skyline keeps dark window marks; all near levels retain sixteen actual recessed arch openings. Original source builder remains preserved; source-local reviewed geometry connects the stair landing and exposes the wooden door in front of its backing.

geographicProposal.notes: Native+Z entrance points north-northeast at heading2.7rad. Inspected north-up Google satellite view shows the projecting canopy/parallel steps on the north-northeast octagonal base, toward the northern keeper compound, rather than the southern slab. APMF2020 entrance photo identifies those forms. Bearing is approximate ±20degrees: trees/parallax/low image resolution preclude a surveyed azimuth; imagery acquisition date is unavailable. limitations: The modeled exterior follows the cited published facts and inspected photographs. Unpublished dimensions and local fittings are explicitly photo-proportioned; no claim of engineering survey accuracy is made.
Portable PBR and shared metric surfaces are provided. Surface weathering, material color under local lighting and fine facade relief require close render review before maximum-detail acceptance.

Paint degradation varies strongly between the2006,2020 and2023 photographs. The model preserves pale shaft/dark upper daymark with reusable plaster and metal surfaces rather than copied stains. Detached keeper houses and island vegetation remain map/environment features; static glazing does not operate a navigational light.
referenceRights: Original geometry and shared procedural materials. Official photographs are research references only; no reference imagery or third-party mesh is embedded or redistributed.
